title: The Wobbly Tune of Tomas's Music Box
markdown:
Tomas loved his little wooden music box, painted with sleepy clouds and friendly stars. When he wound its key, a soft melody played, a lullaby for him and his dog, Sunny. Lately the song sounded different, a gentle hum that made Sunny tilt her head.

“It’s singing a funny song today, Sunny,” he whispered, stroking warm fur. He nudged the winding key. Sunny nudged his hand, tail thumping. When she wagged, he felt a tiny rumble deep in his chest, a tickly vibration. He tapped his marble track; the blue marble rolled slowly.

“Look, Sunny. The track wiggled when I tapped it. The marble moved, like it was dancing.”

Grandpa Lee ambled in, smile warm. “What quiet wonders are you exploring?”

“My music box is making a humming sound, Grandpa. Not its pretty song.”

Grandpa Lee picked it up and showed the small silver cylinder inside, tiny metal teeth. “When these teeth are nudged by this metal comb, they make music. Each bump and wiggle is a note.” Hands on Tomas’s tummy. “Feel this little wiggle?”

Tomas hummed. “Ooooh. My tummy is wiggling! It’s dancing!” The marble track came back. “The track wiggled too! And the marble moved!”

Grandpa Lee smiled. “That’s it. Everything that makes a sound is wiggling. Those tiny bumps travel through the air. That’s what we hear. Your music box’s teeth wiggle to make its song. A tiny orchestra, just for you.”

Tomas looked very carefully. One little tooth was bent, leaning over shyly. “Look! This tooth is crooked! It’s not bumping the comb right. That’s why the wiggles are funny and the song is wobbly!”

Grandpa Lee nodded. “Sometimes a little thing out of place can change the whole tune.” A soft tool. “We just need to persuade this tooth to stand up straight.” Sunny’s head on Tomas’s knee. Grandpa Lee nudged. A tiny almost silent click. Straight.

Tomas’s heart felt light. He wound the key. The cylinder spun. A clear sweet melody, pure and true, the music box’s lovely song, perfectly peaceful. Sunny sighed, tail a gentle rhythm.

“Hooray,” Tomas whispered, hugging the box. “It’s singing its song!”

Grandpa Lee ruffled his hair. Sounds as tiny ripples, things wiggling very fast, waves of sound — he said it once, like a warm blanket, and did not send them hunting every wiggle in the world.

Tomas looked at the box, stars twinkling softly; at Sunny, a happy sleepy woof; at the marble track. He wound the key once more, just to hear the crooked tooth stay brave and straight, and the lullaby came true all the way to the last note.
